main_text.p: ita scripsit. Mustelæ uentriculus Coriandro fartus, & inueteratus comitialibus auxilia turpotus. Item iecur asininum assatum in cibis sumptum ieiuno stomacho. Aliud croci, nardi, ana obolos duos; ueratri nigri {y} obolum unum, scammonij drachmas quatuor, nitri drachmas duas, melle excipito, & drachmas duas ex aqua mulsa bibendas dato. Ciconiæ fimum ex aqua uel oxymeli te propinato. Agarici obolos tres, peuceda ni tantundem, coaguli phocæ, obolum unum, contrita hæc miscentur. Idé author libr. de Materia medica scriptum reliquit, coagulum phocæ epilepticis conferre. Est autem phoca (teste Plinio) marinus vitulus. Et libro tertio afferit Dioscorides, agaricū facere ad morbum comitialem, sumptum trium obolorum pondere. Eundem ait Galenus, libro Simplicium medicamentorum sexto, comitiali morbo obnoxios sanare. Eodem in libro etiam inquit peucedanum utiliter inungi, cum aceto & rosaceo epilepticorum capiti. Oribasius octauo libro ad Euftatium tradit agaricum, semen sesclis, sphodilij radicem, & aristolochiæ rotundæ radicem, ex aqua epotam, comitialibus pdesse. Rutæ sylvestris semen cum aqua potum

page.notes: Text is in a single column with small original sign beside "ueratri nigri" at the right margin (a printed reference mark/annotation, rendered as a blotted symbol). Damaged and faint at the margin; the sign was transcribed as a reference mark only. Upper text is partly cut at the top edge; "ita scripsit" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Some words in the final lines are uncertain at the page-edge fold and the word "sesclis" and "epotam" are read with doubt; the last word "potum" is a line-end fragment. Heavy faint foliage show-through lower left is not transcribed.
